name: Taiyangshou
description: A star 56 parsecs away, 19 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: radius 19.432 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 136.908 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: effective temperature 4482 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.06)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: distance 56.306 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 56 parsecs away, 19 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 137 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,482 K, so 19.432 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 57399: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Chi Ursae Majoris
quotes.card: Chi Ursae Majoris or χ Ursae Majoris, formally named Taiyangshou, is a single star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Major.
quotes.introduction: The star has an orange hue and is visible to the naked eye at night with an apparent visual magnitude of 3.72.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 786420645182229504 (quality A), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
